body.statement:
Suppose that every public real control is represented by an exact dyadic number of encoding length at most \(L_n\).  For every exact dyadic triple \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\in\mathbb D_{L_n}^{n^2+2n}\) and every real triple \((X,R,C)\) in its coordinate box of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\), there is a working precision bounded by a polynomial in \(n,L_n,p_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) such that \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) terminates in bit complexity polynomial in the same quantities and returns \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) containing \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\).  Its certificate satisfies
\[
0\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}})
-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C))
\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}).
\]
It remains valid for repeated retained singular values, computes outward enclosures of \(\Phi^{-1}\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}\) in certified polynomial time, returns the bounded outward fallback hull whenever the spectral gate or retained--discarded split is uncertain, and never silently accepts overflow, a subnormal value, or flush-to-zero behavior.  A refinable non-dyadic control admits the same containment conclusion only after a certified control interval is inserted as input uncertainty; a polynomial bit-complexity corollary additionally requires an explicit uniform time-and-output-size modulus and schedules parameterized by that modulus.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=2^{-p_n-1}\), let \(\mathcal B\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta\), and note that every public control has zero input radius under the proposed exact-dyadic premise.  We construct a coarse branch and a sharp branch.

Let \(T\) be a directed upper bound for every absolute coordinate on \(\mathcal B\), and at a trial working precision \(q\) set
\[
H=n+T+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q+1.
\]
At any point of the box at which \(G_n\) holds,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le{2\over cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2\vee\|Z_{q,n}\|_2\le{\sqrt nT\over\sigma},
\qquad
t_{Z,n}\le{\sqrt{2n}T\over\sigma}=:\overline t.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover \(0<\zeta_\alpha(t)\le z_{\max}:=\Phi^{-1}(1-3\alpha/8)\).  Define
\[
\overline R=\sqrt{C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+2\overline t+A_{r,\alpha})}
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\overline W={2\over cn}
\left\{z_{\max}(\overline t+\overline R)
+{C_{r,\alpha}\over2}\log(e+\overline t+\overline R)\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The definitions and monotonicity give \(W_n\le\overline W\).  Also
\[
|\widehat\theta_n|=|RX_r^+C|\le{2T^2\over c},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
d_n\le K_0\sigma^2\ell_n n^{-2}
\left({\sqrt nT\over\sigma}+\sqrt{\ell_n}\right)^2=:\overline d.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus every feasible on-gate interval is contained in
\[
[-\overline H,\overline H],
\qquad
\overline H={2T^2\over c}+\sigma^2\overline W+\overline d,
\tag{6}
\]
whereas every off-gate interval is \([-M_0,M_0]\).  Directed versions of (1)--(6) are computable without a spectral gap.  Replacing logarithms and square roots by the elementary majorants above shows that their magnitudes and exponent encodings are polynomial in the input bit lengths.  Hence the hull of (6) and the fallback is a certified coarse enclosure.

For the sharp branch use the invariant projectors
\[
P_R=\mathbf1_{((cn/2)^2,\infty)}(X^{\top}X),
\qquad
P_L=\mathbf1_{((cn/2)^2,\infty)}(XX^{\top}).
\tag{7}
\]
When the certified count above the threshold is \(r\),
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\top}(X_rX_r^{\top}+I-P_L)^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]
To verify (8), substitute a compact SVD \(X_r=U_rS_rV_r^{\top}\); the inverse is \(U_rS_r^{-2}U_r^{\top}+I-P_L\), and left multiplication by \(X_r^{\top}\) gives \(V_rS_r^{-1}U_r^{\top}\).

The proved proposed version of \(\textnormal{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) supplies a polynomial-time inverse candidate for every inverse in the sign iteration and (8): after symmetrization it uses
\[
L_{k+1}=L_k(2I-\widehat K L_k),
\qquad L_0=\widehat K/\Lambda^2,
\tag{9}
\]
and the directly checked residual satisfies the solved recurrence \(r_{k+1}\le r_k^2+CH^d2^{-q}\).  Its proof shows that (9) reaches residual \(O(H^{d'}2^{-q})\) in \(O(\log H+\log(q+2))\) steps, with candidate norm at most \(2\|\widehat K^{-1}\|\).  For the sign iteration it also proves the noncommutative enclosure recurrence
\[
R_{j+1}\le{3\over2}R_j+CH^d2^{1-q}
\tag{10}
\]
and adds to the final projector radius the exact tail
\[
{\chi^{2^J}\over1-\chi^{2^J}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (9)--(11) give both residual validity and polynomial bit complexity, rather than relying on an unspecified inverse oracle.  The exact endpoint depends only on
\[
RX_r^+C,quad
{1\over\sigma}\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+\|(X_r^+)^{\top}R^{\top}\|_2^2},quad
{\|P_RR^{\top}\|_2\over\sigma},quad
{\|P_LC\|_2\over\sigma}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus rotations inside a repeated retained singular space change no endpoint.  A boundary tie is not accepted and invokes the coarse hull.

It remains to justify special functions and termination.  Repeated integration gives, for \(x\ge0\),
\[
F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)=1-e^{-x/2}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}{(x/2)^j\over j!}.
\tag{13}
\]
Taylor's formula with its integral remainder gives
\[
\left|e^y-\sum_{j=0}^m{y^j\over j!}\right|
\le{e^{|y|}|y|^{m+1}\over(m+1)!},
\tag{14}
\]
and the Gaussian identity
\[
\Phi(x)={1\over2}+{1\over\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_0^xe^{-t^2/2}\,dt
\tag{15}
\]
has a directed rational evaluation of polynomial cost.  Explicitly, enclose \(\pi\) with Machin's identity
\[
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\]
and the alternating series for \(\arctan\); \(O(s)\) terms give \(s\) certified bits.  Directed bisection then encloses \(\sqrt{2\pi}\).  On a bracket \(|x|\le X\), integrate the exponential Taylor polynomial termwise in (15); the remainder (14) shows that \(O(s+X^2+1)\) terms give \(s\) bits after binary range reduction.  All numerator and exponent lengths are polynomial in \(s\) and the bit length of \(X\).  The Chernoff calculation
\[
P(Z\ge x)\le\inf_{t>0}e^{-tx+t^2/2}=e^{-x^2/2}
\tag{16}
\]
provides a normal-quantile bracket of polynomial bit length, and (13) provides one of size \(O_{r_0}(1+\log(1/\gamma))\) at upper-tail probability \(\gamma\).  Because the densities are positive on finite interior brackets, directed probability-bracketed bisection returns an interval containing each quantile \(Q\) with width at most
\[
8\,2^{1-q}(1+|Q|).
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (13)--(17) use polynomially many operations in the requested precision, the input lengths, and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), since \(r\le r_0\) is fixed.

At successively doubled precisions up to
\[
q^\star=8\{n+L_n+p_n+\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil+1\}^2,
\tag{18}
\]
attempt the certified off-gate or common-split on-gate branch.  If neither succeeds, return the coarse hull.  There are \(O(\log q^\star)\) attempts.  Each attempt uses the explicit matrix iterations (9)--(11), polynomially many \(n\)-dimensional operations, and the scalar bisections above.  Mantissas and all stored exponent encodings have polynomial length.  This proves termination and polynomial bit complexity.

For a fixed \((X,R,C)\in\mathcal B\), write its exact interval as \([L,U]\) and the returned interval as \([\underline L,\overline U]\).  The recurrence induction, residual test, quantile brackets, and hull rule prove
\[
\underline L\le L\le U\le\overline U.
\tag{19}
\]
Endpointwise propagation gives
\[
0\le L-\underline L\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}},
\qquad
0\le\overline U-U\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}.
\tag{20}
\]
Adding (20) proves the length inequality.  Arbitrary-precision signed exponents exclude overflow and subnormals in the abstract model; the stated IEEE route emits no certificate unless rescaling and exponent widening exclude overflow, subnormal values, and flushing.  Finally, a supplied control interval can be inserted with half-width as input radius, but its production cost is not bounded without the additional uniform modulus stated in the proposed claim.  This proves the corrected certificate.
body.justification: This theorem gives a worst-case outward certificate on exact dyadic data and every real observation in its preimage box, including repeated singular values and uncertain gates.
body.gap: Polynomial complexity is proved for exact-dyadic public controls; a refinable non-dyadic control requires a separately supplied uniform time-and-output-size modulus.
body.consumer: Interval-library implementations can audit containment independently of the Gaussian sampling argument.
